chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Saffar al-Nahawandi narrated to us in it, saying: Abu al-Faraj Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khuzay al-Samiri narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim al-Qantari narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-Halwani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sari narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:

Follow the sun, and if the sun sets, follow the moon, and if the moon sets, follow Venus (al-Zuhra), and if Venus sets, follow the two Farqads (stars). Then they said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the sun? And what is the moon? And what is Venus? And what are the two Farqads? So he said: I am the Sun, Ali is the Moon, Venus is Fatima, and the Two Farqads are Hasan and Husayn.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْفَرْقَدَانِ: The two Farqad stars (metaphor for Hasan and Husayn)

ai.seo_question: Who are the Sun, Moon, Venus, and Farqads in this Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith employs a celestial metaphor to establish the spiritual hierarchy of the Ahl al-Bayt, positioning the Prophet as the guiding Sun and the Imams as subsequent luminaries. This narration underscores the concept of *Nur* (light) in Shia theology, illustrating how divine guidance transitions through the progeny of the Prophet, with the 'two Farqads' specifically highlighting the dual role of Hasan and Husayn as enduring stars of leadership.
